es: Interpretar indirectas, atenuaciones (not bad, a bit late) e ironía en textos y audios breves, identificando la pista que revela la intención.

vocabulary.es: atenuación, decir menos de lo que es

teaching.en: After the flood, Tom looked at the ruined kitchen and said with a straight face, 'We have a small problem', a classic understatement.
teaching.es: Después de la inundación, Tom miró la cocina destrozada y dijo con cara seria: «Tenemos un pequeño problema», una atenuación clásica.
teaching.explanationEs: El understatement dice menos de lo que es; with a straight face hace la broma más difícil de detectar.
segments: After the flood, Tom looked at the ruined kitchen and said with
a straight face, 'We have a small problem', a classic understatement.
teaching.audioText: After the flood, Tom looked at the ruined kitchen and said with a straight face, 'We have a small problem', a classic understatement.

teaching.en: 'You're a bit late,' said the boss to Leo, who had arrived two hours after the meeting started, and she used the phrase to downplay a serious problem.
teaching.es: «Llegas un poco tarde», dijo la jefa a Leo, que había llegado dos horas después de empezar la reunión, y usó la frase para quitar importancia a un problema serio.
teaching.explanationEs: Downplay es restar importancia; aquí a bit convierte dos horas en algo casi insignificante.
segments: 'You're a bit late,' said the boss to Leo, who had arrived two hours
after the meeting started, and she used the phrase to downplay a serious problem.
teaching.audioText: 'You're a bit late,' said the boss to Leo, who had arrived two hours after the meeting started, and she used the phrase to downplay a serious problem.

teaching.en: 'What a brilliant idea,' said Mia in a sarcastic voice when the plan failed, and nobody in the room thought that she meant it.
teaching.es: «Qué idea tan genial», dijo Mia con voz sarcástica cuando el plan falló, y nadie en la sala pensó que lo dijera en serio.
teaching.explanationEs: Brilliant es positivo en literal; sarcastic indica que quiere decir lo contrario.
segments: 'What a brilliant idea,' said Mia in a sarcastic voice when the
plan failed, and nobody in the room thought that she meant it.
teaching.audioText: 'What a brilliant idea,' said Mia in a sarcastic voice when the plan failed, and nobody in the room thought that she meant it.

teaching.en: The irony is that the cooking teacher burned the dinner, and he described it in a deadpan tone as 'a small mistake'.
teaching.es: La ironía es que el profesor de cocina quemó la cena, y lo describió con gesto impasible como «un pequeño error».
teaching.explanationEs: La irony es la diferencia entre lo esperado y lo ocurrido; deadpan es decirlo sin mostrar emoción.
segments: The irony is that the cooking teacher burned the dinner, and
he described it in a deadpan tone as 'a small mistake'.
teaching.audioText: The irony is that the cooking teacher burned the dinner, and he described it in a deadpan tone as 'a small mistake'.

teaching.en: The critic called the concert 'not bad', which is high praise from him, although his tongue in cheek style makes it easy to miss.
teaching.es: El crítico calificó el concierto de «no está mal», lo cual es un gran elogio viniendo de él, aunque su estilo en broma hace fácil no notarlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Tongue in cheek indica que algo se dice en broma o con sorna; aquí not bad es elogio, no crítica.
segments: The critic called the concert 'not bad', which is high praise from
him, although his tongue in cheek style makes it easy to miss.
teaching.audioText: The critic called the concert 'not bad', which is high praise from him, although his tongue in cheek style makes it easy to miss.

teaching.en: A sarcastic remark is sharper than understatement, because the speaker wants the listener to feel the criticism behind the joke.
teaching.es: Un comentario sarcástico es más cortante que la atenuación, porque el hablante quiere que el oyente sienta la crítica que hay tras la broma.
teaching.explanationEs: Comparar ayuda a clasificar: la atenuación suaviza, el sarcasmo hiere y la ironía contrasta.
segments: A sarcastic remark is sharper than understatement, because the speaker
wants the listener to feel the criticism behind the joke.
teaching.audioText: A sarcastic remark is sharper than understatement, because the speaker wants the listener to feel the criticism behind the joke.

prompt.es: Elige qué quiere decir de verdad el profesor con su frase.

choices.text: It is only a small problem that will soon be solved.
It is a serious problem that he chooses to downplay.
It is a funny surprise that he is enjoying.

feedback.es: El aula inundada y la ventana rota contradicen a bit of a problem: el profesor usa una atenuación para quitar importancia a algo grave.

hint.es: Compara las palabras con los hechos: ¿encaja «un poco» con el desastre descrito?

origin.text: During a storm, the teacher looks at the flooded classroom and the broken window and says calmly, 'Well, that is a bit of a problem.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Decir «no está mal» de una película increíble es una atenuación.»

feedback.es: Understatement es decir menos de lo que se piensa: not bad ante una película increíble es un caso típico.

hint.es: Es el nombre de la figura que dice menos de lo que es.

origin.text: Saying 'not bad' about an amazing film is an ___, because it says much less than you really think.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La ironía es que el panadero nunca come pan.»

answer.text: The irony is that the baker never eats bread

feedback.es: The irony is that introduce un contraste entre lo esperado (un panadero come pan) y lo que ocurre.

hint.es: Empieza por The irony is that.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige cómo va realmente la mañana de la jefa.

choices.text: Perfectly: she is happy to welcome a new colleague.
Slowly: she is not interested in anything today.
Badly: she describes a crisis as a minor problem.

feedback.es: La impresora en llamas y el cliente gritando contradicen «a small problem»: la jefa atenúa una crisis para no dejarse llevar por el pánico.

origin.audio: Yesterday my new boss introduced me to the team. The printer had just caught fire, the client was shouting on the phone, and she turned to me and said, calmly, Welcome to the company. Just a small problem this morning. Later she admitted that she always downplays things when she is under pressure, because panic makes everything worse. I couldn't help laughing; it was the most honest welcome I've ever had.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opinó realmente el vecino del concierto.

choices.text: He found it boring and wanted to leave.
He loved it so much that he lost track of time.
He found it exciting but could not find his seat.

feedback.es: Decir que fueron las mejores dos horas de la semana, con gesto impasible y buscando la salida, es ironía: el concierto le pareció aburrido.

origin.audio: I asked my neighbour whether he enjoyed the concert. He said, deadpan, Oh, it was the best two hours of my week, although I spent most of them looking for the exit.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su significado real.

pairs.es: Elogio suave: en realidad está muy bien
Ironía: la idea fue un desastre

pairs: He said it with a straight face.

feedback.es: Las cuatro frases dicen una cosa y significan otra: elogio moderado, atenuación, ironía y broma con gesto serio.

pairs.es: Elogio suave: en realidad está muy bien
Ironía: la idea fue un desastre

pairs: He said it with a straight face.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué piensa realmente el hermano de la tarta.

choices.text: He thinks it is nothing special, but he is polite.
He thinks it is very good, but he downplays it.
He thinks it is too sweet, although he ate it.

feedback.es: Tres trozos, dos más a escondidas y la frase final sobre su fama de criticarlo todo muestran que not bad es una atenuación de algo muy positivo.

origin.audio: When I asked my brother whether he liked my cake, he smiled and said, It's not bad. I pointed out that he had eaten three pieces, so he admitted, with a smile, that he had also taken two more to the kitchen when he thought I wasn't looking. From a boy who usually criticises everything, that was high praise.

prompt.es: Con el mismo relato, elige qué hecho contradice sus palabras «it's not bad».

choices.text: He smiled while he answered the question.
He said that the cake was very sweet.
He secretly took two more pieces to the kitchen.

feedback.es: Llevarse dos trozos más a escondidas es el hecho que desmiente su frase: nadie repite tanto de una tarta que solo considera pasable.

prompt.es: Completa: «Dijo «qué idea tan genial» con voz sarcástica.»

feedback.es: Sarcastic describe la voz de quien dice lo contrario de lo que piensa para criticar; que nadie se riera lo confirma.

origin.text: When the plan failed, she said, 'What a brilliant idea!' in a ___ voice, and nobody laughed.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Un chiste con cara seria puede ser difícil de notar.»

answer.text: A deadpan joke can be hard to notice

feedback.es: Deadpan describe el humor sin gesto ni emoción, por eso cuesta distinguirlo de una frase dicha en serio.

prompt.es: Lee la escena. ¿Qué quiere decir de verdad la hermana con «Well done»?

choices.text: That he has made a mistake, and she is being ironic.
That he handled a difficult situation very well.
That she wants him to bake another cake.

feedback.es: La tarta en el suelo y los brazos cruzados contradicen el elogio: Well done es una ironía que subraya el error.

origin.text: At the family party, Carlos carries the birthday cake to the table, trips over the dog and drops it on the floor. His sister looks at the mess, folds her arms and says, 'Well done.'

prompt.es: Escucha la reseña y elige qué opinión real transmite el crítico.

choices.text: A positive opinion hidden behind simple words.
A negative opinion softened by understatement.
A plain account with no opinion at all.

feedback.es: Un poco alto y marcharse antes porque le dolían los oídos delatan que not bad y a bit loud suavizan una opinión negativa.

origin.audio: The review said, The singer was not bad, and the band was a bit loud. In the same paragraph the reviewer wrote that he had to leave early because his ears hurt.

prompt.es: Completa: «Viniendo de un crítico que lo odia todo, «not bad» es un gran elogio.»

feedback.es: High praise es elogio enorme: el contexto (un crítico que lo odia todo) hace que not bad valga como aplauso.

origin.text: From a critic who hates everything, 'not bad' is high ___.
